subject: Parliament of India (Sansad Bhavan)
motif: Illustrates the majestic circular colonnade architecture of the historic Parliament House building.
details: Sansad Bhavan is the iconic seat of the Parliament of India in New Delhi. Designed by British architects Sir Edwin Lutyens and Sir Herbert Baker, it was inaugurated in 1927. The cancellation celebrates India's vibrant democracy.

subject: Rashtrapati Bhavan (Presidential Residence)
motif: Line drawing of the central dome and front facade of the Rashtrapati Bhavan.
details: Rashtrapati Bhavan is the official residence of the President of India at the western end of Rajpath in New Delhi. It features a massive 340-room main building combining classical Greco-Roman and Indian architectural elements.

subject: Red Fort (Lal Qila)
motif: Depicts the Lahore Gate ramparts and octagonal sandstone towers of the UNESCO World Heritage Red Fort.
details: Built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in 1638 when he shifted his capital from Agra to Delhi. Red Fort symbolizes Indian independence, where the Prime Minister hoists the national flag every Independence Day.

subject: Peacock (Philately Logo)
motif: Features the stylized national bird Peacock holding a envelope stamp emblem.
details: Located at Dak Bhawan on Parliament Street, the National Philatelic Museum houses rare Indian postal stamps, first-day covers, and historical postal archives operated by Department of Posts.

subject: Himalayan Monal (State Bird)
motif: Depicts the iridescent-crested Himalayan Monal pheasant perched on a pine branch.
details: The Himalayan Monal (Lophophorus impejanus) is the state bird of Himachal Pradesh. Renowned for its brilliant metallic multicolored plumage, it inhabits high-altitude oak-conifer forests of the Himalayas.

subject: World's Highest Post Office
motif: Depicts the traditional mud-brick Hikkim Post Office structure against snowy Spiti peaks.
details: Situated at an altitude of 14,567 feet (4,440 m) in the Spiti Valley, Hikkim is world-famous as the highest functioning post office in the world, receiving thousands of traveler postcards annually.

subject: Tabo Monastery (Ajanta of the Himalayas)
motif: Features the ancient stupa mud-facade structure of Tabo Gompa.
details: Founded in 996 AD by Tibetan Buddhist translator Rinchen Zangpo, Tabo Monastery is renowned for its invaluable collection of frescoes, manuscripts, and statues preserved in high desert cold climate.

subject: Sri Hadimba Devi Temple
motif: Features four-tiered wooden pagoda roof architecture surrounded by Dhungri deodar forests.
details: Built in 1553 AD by Maharaja Bahadur Singh, this cave temple is dedicated to Hadimba Devi, wife of Bhima from the epic Mahabharata. It is famous for intricate wooden carvings and pagoda roof.

subject: Himalayas & Paragliding in Bir Billing
motif: Paraglider soaring over the snow-capped Dhauladhar Himalayan range.
details: Bir Billing in Kangra district is globally acclaimed as the Paragliding Capital of India and host of Paragliding World Cups, offering stunning views of Dhauladhar mountain peaks.

subject: Asian Elephant (Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary)
motif: Tusked Asian Elephant wading in Periyar lake waters.
details: Periyar National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary in Thekkady is a premier elephant and tiger reserve situated high in the Cardamom Hills of the Western Ghats.

subject: Holy Eighteen Steps (Patinettam Padi) - Sabarimala
motif: Holy 18 gold-plated steps leading to the sanctum sanctorum of Lord Ayyappa temple.
details: Sabarimala is one of the world's largest annual pilgrimage sites, attracting millions of devotees. The Post Office operates seasonally during the Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage period.

subject: Bekal Fort & Keyhole Tower
motif: Observation keyhole tower overlooking the Arabian Sea coastline.
details: Bekal Fort is the largest sea fort in Kerala, built by Shivappa Nayaka of Keladi in 1650 AD. Its strategic coastline positioning features a keyhole-shaped layout and grand water tank.

subject: Magen David - Paradesi Synagogue
motif: Six-pointed Star of David symbol of the historic Paradesi Synagogue.
details: Constructed in 1568 by Spanish-speaking Sephardic Jews, the Paradesi Synagogue in Mattancherry (Kochi) is the oldest active synagogue in the Commonwealth of Nations, famous for hand-painted Chinese willow tiles.

subject: Aranmula Snake Boat & Metal Mirror (Kannadi)
motif: Traditional Palliyodam snake boat alongside the famous Aranmula metal mirror outline.
details: Aranmula on Pamba River is globally famous for the Aranmula Uthrattathi Boat Race and the GI-tagged Aranmula Kannadi—a unique front-surface metal-alloy mirror made using secret traditional metalworking craft.

subject: Brihadeeswarar Temple (Big Temple)
motif: Vimana tower and Nandi pavilion of the UNESCO World Heritage Chola Temple.
details: Built by Emperor Raja Raja Chola I in 1010 AD, Brihadeeswarar Temple is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture featuring a massive 216 ft granite vimana tower topped by an 80-ton single stone capstone.

subject: Vivekananda Rock Memorial & Thiruvalluvar Statue
motif: Rock island memorial twin structures at the confluence of Indian Ocean, Arabian Sea, and Bay of Bengal.
details: Located on a offshore rock island where Swami Vivekananda meditated in 1892, alongside the 133-foot tall stone statue of Tamil philosopher-poet Thiruvalluvar.

subject: Shore Temple & Pancha Rathas
motif: Structural coastal stone Shore Temple of Mamallapuram.
details: Built by Pallava King Narasimhavarman II in the 8th century AD, Mahabalipuram is famous for monolithic rock-cut cave temples and shore temple architectural sculptures.

subject: Indian Gaur (Bison)
motif: Profile depiction of the massive Indian Gaur (Bos gaurus).
details: Mudumalai National Park and Tiger Reserve in Nilgiris is a vital sanctuary connecting Western Ghats wildlife corridors home to gaurs, elephants, and Bengal tigers.

subject: Stone Chariot at Vittala Temple
motif: The world-famous Stone Chariot (Garuda Shrine) of Hampi.
details: Hampi was the majestic capital of the Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th century. The Stone Chariot at Vittala Temple complex is an iconic symbol of Indian heritage featured on the ₹50 currency note.

subject: Darpana Sundari (Shilabalika)
motif: Carved soapstone Shilabalika maiden admiring herself in a mirror.
details: Chennakeshava Temple at Belur was commissioned by Hoysala King Vishnuvardhana in 1117 AD. The temple exterior contains 42 bracket figures (Shilabalikas) showcasing exceptional ancient stone sculpture finesse.

subject: Lord Gommateshwara (Bahubali Statue)
motif: 57-foot monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali standing on Vindhyagiri hill.
details: Carved from single granite block in 981 AD under Western Ganga Dynasty minister Chavundaraya. It is one of the largest free-standing monolithic statues in the world, venue of Mahamastakabhisheka.

subject: Indian Sloth Bear
motif: Indian Sloth Bear amidst rocky scrub hills.
details: Daroji Sloth Bear Sanctuary near Hampi was created in 1994 specifically for the protection of native Indian Sloth Bears (Melursus ursinus) in Deccan thorn scrub forest habitats.

subject: Six-Tusked Elephant / Cave Entrance
motif: Six-tusked elephant Jataka story motif and Cave 19 facade.
details: Ajanta Caves feature 30 rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments dating from 2nd century BCE to 480 CE. Famous worldwide for exquisite ancient frescoes and murals illustrating Jataka tales.

subject: Kailasha Temple Carved Pillars (Cave 16)
motif: Monolithic monolithic carved elephant and pillars of Kailash Temple.
details: Cave 16 (Kailasha Temple) is the largest single monolithic rock excavation in the world, carved top-down out of basalt cliff face under Rashtrakuta King Krishna I in the 8th century.

subject: Gateway of India & GPO Heritage Dome
motif: Indo-Saracenic arch of Gateway of India and Mumbai GPO central dome.
details: Gateway of India was built to commemorate the landing of King George V in 1911. Mumbai GPO is an architectural marvel designed by John Begg in 1913 inspired by Bijapur's Gol Gumbaz.

subject: Greater Flamingo (Thane Creek Sanctuary)
motif: Flock of long-necked Greater Flamingos feeding in mudflats.
details: Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary is a vital urban wetland habitat in Navi Mumbai where tens of thousands of migratory flamingos gather every winter season.

subject: Mahatma Gandhi & Charkha
motif: Mahatma Gandhi's spinning wheel (Charkha) and Hriday Kunj cottage.
details: Sabarmati Ashram on the banks of Sabarmati River served as the headquarters of Mahatma Gandhi during India's freedom movement from 1917 to 1930, launch site of historic Dandi Salt March.

subject: Asiatic Lion (Gir Forest)
motif: Roaring Asiatic Lion male head profile.
details: Gir National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary is the sole natural home of the endangered Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) in the world, established in 1965.

subject: Indian Wild Ass (Khur)
motif: Indian Wild Ass galloping across Little Rann of Kutch salt flats.
details: The Wild Ass Sanctuary in Little Rann of Kutch is the last refuge of the endangered Indian Wild Ass (Equus hemionus khur), known locally as Khur.

subject: Sidi Saiyyed Jali (Tree of Life)
motif: Intricate stone latticework window depicting intertwining tree branches.
details: Built in 1572 AD, the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque is famed for its ten stone pier carved windows (jalis), serving as an unofficial symbol of Ahmedabad city and logo of IIM Ahmedabad.

subject: Great Stupa of Sanchi & Torana Gateway
motif: Sanchi Stupa dome and carved stone Torana gateway.
details: One of the oldest stone structures in India, commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in 3rd century BCE. Sanchi Stupa was among the first permanent pictorial postmarks created in independent India.

subject: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple
motif: Shikhara spire and sculptural friezes of Kandariya Mahadeva Temple.
details: Khajuraho Group of Monuments were built by Chandela Dynasty between 950 and 1050 AD. Celebrated for Nagara-style architecture and exquisite expressive sculptures.

subject: Prehistoric Cave Paintings
motif: Rock painting outline of ancient hunter riding horse holding spear.
details: Bhimbetka rock shelters exhibit the earliest traces of human life in India, featuring Mesolithic hunter-gatherer cave paintings dating back over 10,000 years.

subject: Sonar Quila (Golden Fort)
motif: Yellow sandstone fort bastions rising above Thar desert dunes.
details: Built in 1156 AD by Rajput ruler Rawal Jaisal, Jaisalmer Fort is one of the few living forts in the world, home to one-fourth of the city's population inside its golden walls.

subject: Siberian Crane & Migratory Waterfowl
motif: Pair of Siberian Cranes amidst wetland reeds.
details: Keoladeo National Park (formerly Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary) is a world-renowned wintering ground for thousands of waterfowl and rare migratory birds.

subject: Lake Palace (Jag Niwas) - Lake Pichola
motif: White marble palace floating on Lake Pichola waters.
details: Built between 1743 and 1746 by Maharana Jagat Singh II as a summer palace, Jag Niwas is a breathtaking example of Mewar royal architecture.

subject: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train)
motif: Steam engine narrow-gauge Toy Train winding around Batasia Loop.
details: Built between 1879 and 1881, the DHR Toy Train is a UNESCO World Heritage site operating on 2-foot narrow gauge tracks climbing through Himalayan tea gardens.

subject: Visva-Bharati & Rabindranath Tagore
motif: Upasana Griha (Prayer Hall) glass structure and Tagore portrait emblem.
details: Santiniketan was founded by Maharshi Debendranath Tagore and expanded by Nobel Laureate Rabindranath Tagore into Visva-Bharati University, recently named a UNESCO World Heritage site.

subject: Sun Temple Chariot Wheel (Konark)
motif: Intricately carved stone sundial chariot wheel of Konark.
details: Built in 1250 AD by Eastern Ganga King Narasimhadeva I, Konark Sun Temple is designed in the shape of a colossal 24-wheeled stone chariot pulled by seven horses.

subject: Lord Jagannath Temple & Rath Yatra Chariot
motif: Nandighosa chariot dome and temple Neelachakra wheel.
details: 12th-century sacred temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath, famous worldwide for its annual Rath Yatra (Chariot Festival) attracting millions of devotees.

subject: Great One-Horned Rhinoceros
motif: One-horned rhino grazing in elephant grass marshes.
details: Kaziranga National Park hosts two-thirds of the world's Great One-Horned Rhinoceros population along the floodplains of the Brahmaputra River.

subject: Living Root Bridges & Nohkalikai Falls
motif: Double-decker bio-engineered Ficus root bridge over mountain stream.
details: Sohra (Cherrapunji) is famous for receiving some of the highest rainfall on Earth and for its living root bridges grown by Khasi tribes from rubber fig tree roots.

subject: Cellular Jail National Memorial
motif: Central watchtower and radiating cell wings of Cellular Jail (Kala Pani).
details: Colonial prison used by the British to exile Indian freedom fighters. Constructed between 1896 and 1906, it stands today as a national memorial monument.

subject: Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple)
motif: Golden sanctum reflection in Amrit Sarovar lake waters.
details: The holiest Gurdwara of Sikhism, founded by Guru Ram Das in 1577. Its golden leaf foil superstructure was built by Maharaja Ranjit Singh in 1830.

subject: Open Hand Monument & Zakir Rose Garden
motif: Le Corbusier's Open Hand sculpture and Shivalik Hills backdrop.
details: Designed by architect Le Corbusier as a symbol of 'peace, reconciliation, and openness to give and receive', standing 26 meters high.

subject: Ganga Ghats & Evening Aarti
motif: River ghat steps, temples, and traditional river boats on the Ganges.
details: Varanasi (Kashi) is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, spiritual heart of Hinduism famed for ancient ghats along the sacred Ganges River.

subject: Kedarnath Temple & Himalayan Peaks
motif: Stone Kedarnath Temple structure backed by snow-clad Kedarnath peak.
details: Located at 3,583 meters altitude near the Mandakini River, Kedarnath is one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva and key part of Char Dham Yatra.
